data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism's central assertion that acting on the best-tested theory is 'the only rational strategy to approximate truth, even without ... an inductive inference that the future will resemble the past' is question-begging. To label past severe testing as a rational guide to *approximating truth* (a forward-looking claim about which theory is closer to the truth) one must assume that surviving past tests is positively correlated with future truth-likeness. That correlation is precisely the inductive inference the target denies making. Relabeling it as a 'methodological rule' does not eliminate the inductive dependency; it conceals it. The claim of being non-inductive is therefore circular, not established.
